messages:
Alex: Quick Q — I'm seeing a contract mismatch between the REST /generate endpoint and both Python/TS SDKs. REST accepts `max_tokens` (int) and defaults to 256, but the Python SDK sends `maxTokens` and omits the field when None which triggers a 512 default server-side. Repro: 
Alex: REST payload we send from curl:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "prompt": "hi",
  "max_tokens": 256
}
```
Alex: Python SDK call:
```
client.generate(prompt="hi")  # no max_tokens param set
```
Alex: TS SDK call:
```
client.generate({ prompt: 'hi', maxTokens: 256 })
```
Maddy: ugh, that explains the token spikes we saw in prod yesterday :grimacing:
Maddy: The TypeScript SDK maps param names to camelCase (maxTokens) and explicitly serializes values. Python uses snake_case but has optional default argument = None, so it intentionally omits the key when not provided. Server default changed in a release last month from 256 -> 512 which made the difference visible.
Ryan: I dug in — server accepts both names (`max_tokens` and `maxTokens`) but prioritizes `max_tokens` if present. The Python omission means server uses new global default. We should either: 1) make Python send explicit default (256) in client, 2) server fallback should prefer previous default for backwards compat, or 3) document breaking change.
Kim: Option 1 seems safest and least surprising. Is that a breaking change for anyone relying on 512?
Alex: Probably not many, but still risky to silently change behavior. Proposal: ship a patch that makes Python SDK include `max_tokens` when param is None (set to client default 256), and add a toggle env var to opt into server new default.
Maddy: fine by me. Also noticed serialization mismatch for `metadata` field: Python encodes dicts as JSON strings in query param, TS sends nested JSON body. Some endpoints expect an object, others parse string -> JSON. That's been causing flaky filtering.
Ryan: Good catch — example server log shows: `received metadata: "{"user":"u1"}"` vs `received metadata: {user: 'u1'}`. We should standardize to always send JSON body `metadata` as object, not string.
Kim: Agree. Also, what about datetime? REST accepts ISO8601 but Python SDK used `datetime.timestamp()` (float secs). Could break webhook matching.
Alex: Yep. Need consistency: SDKs should serialize datetimes to RFC3339/ISO8601 strings. Add a test in integration suite to assert roundtrip.
Ryan: I'll open a PR to enforce serialization and default behavior after this thread. Drafting changes now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432 (WIP)
Maddy: Can you add a changelog note and a compatibility section in README about the explicit defaults?
Ryan: Will do. Also adding a small migration guide for anyone relying on server-side defaults.
CI-Bot: deploy/presubmit status: SDK unit tests: 142 passed, 3 skipped, 4 failed (serialization tests) — https://ci.local/jobs/987
Alex: ok let's target a patch release. Ryan, can you add a compatibility flag and tests by EOD? If not, we'll hotfix server to temporarily restore old default.
Ryan: on it. Will ping when PR is ready for review.
Kim: Thx — and please @product if this changes visible default behavior for public API customers.
Maddy: tagging @product in the docs thread. :thumbsup:
Alex: thanks all. Follow-ups: Ryan (PR + tests), Maddy (docs changelog), Kim (prod comms).
